To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
participants were able to learn within-modal and within-category dependencies, but not cross-modal or cross-category dependencies.
cross-modal and cross-category dependencies are more difficult to learn than within-modal and within-category dependencies.
individuals are able to learn statistical dependencies within a modality or perceptual category but not across modalities or perceptual categories.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the ability of the human perceptual system to learn cross-domain statistical–sequential dependencies, and how these cross-domain dependencies are learned in a multimodal and/or multichannel environment.
the ability of individuals to learn sequential dependencies in a cross-modal environment and how the perceptual categories of the stimuli influence the effectiveness of this learning.
the question of how the brain is capable of extracting statistical information from a complex environment and how this information is used to guide behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cross-domain dependencies are difficult to learn, but not impossible.
cross-modal statistical learning is difficult, but not impossible, to achieve.

the human brain has the capacity to learn cross-modal statistical dependencies, but that these capacities are limited by modality constraints that restrict the ability to learn cross-domain statistical dependencies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cross-domain statistical–sequential dependencies are difficult to learn.
the learning of cross-domain sequential dependencies is difficult, and that the difficulty is modality-specific.
the learning of statistical–sequential dependencies is difficult to achieve in a cross-domain environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cross-modal and cross-category learning is difficult and that the brain may not be able to learn these types of dependencies when they occur sequentially.
cross-modal and cross-category learning of statistical–sequential dependencies is not an easy task, and that it requires additional processing resources and/or more exposure to a stimulus sequence.
the learning of sequential statistical dependencies across modalities or perceptual categories is more difficult than learning within a single domain or modality.
